chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: How Ella learned new songs
summary: Ella heard the arrangement run down, took lyric cards home, and returned having memorized them; many songs were turned down.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And we'd try to add some little gimmick into them, or we just show -- we got this little thing in here, little thing in there, and run the arrangements.

She'd hear the arrangements go down. She says, "Okay, let's go." And she'd sing it, and (Inaudible) so I say let's go to the next one. And she come back the night -- Didn't use no music. She's got it! Her lyrics. We didn't stand up in front of the mike with no music!

When she went over a song in rehearsal, she had cards. Maybe she could take the cards home with her, you know. Just sing the song down and she'd go home and memorize the lyrics. And when she came back the night when we were going to play the arrangements -- rehearse that day, perfect. Wouldn't be no stumbling or I forgot the lyrics. I never heard her say I forgot the lyrics or nothing. When she do a song, it was just down.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
That's it. And it's a lot of songs that we pulled for her, now. A lot of songs that people brought to her never made the book. They were turned down.
She would turn down some and we would turn down some.
(Inaudible) wouldn't turn them down because they had to get by us anyway. She know that.
